transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I, um... well, it’s a lot of things, really, but I suppose the main reason I’m sitting here today is that things have just gotten so incredibly heavy lately, and it’s started to scare me. I work as a veterinary technologist, and I’ve been at my current clinic for a long time. I have my graduate degree, I know what I'm doing, and usually, I can handle the stress of the job, you know? We see a lot of tough cases, but I've always managed. 

But lately, the days just drag on and on, and I come home completely drained in a way I can't even fully describe. And what actually scared me enough to finally pick up the phone and make this appointment—because I really did put it off for weeks, trying to convince myself I was just burnt out or needing a vacation—is that I keep having these really dark thoughts that I can't shake. Every single night when I go to sleep, I just keep thinking that it would be so much easier if I just didn’t wake up. Just... peace, you know? No more alarms, no more having to force myself out of bed to do it all over again. 

And then it started happening outside of bed, too. Sometimes when I’m driving home from the clinic—it's a fairly long commute, especially with the traffic, and there are these sharp curves on the highway—I actually catch myself staring at the concrete dividers and wondering what would happen if I just didn't turn the wheel. Like, if I just let the car keep going straight and just let whatever happens, happen. It just pops into my head, and it’s terrifying to realize I’m actually contemplating it, just sitting there in the driver's seat feeling completely detached from whether I make it home or not. So I just knew I had to come in and talk to someone before I actually let go of the wheel one of these days.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things anymore—things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, time with friends or family, or even small everyday moments?

Yes... yes, actually, that's exactly it. It's like all the color has just been drained out of everything. I used to have all these things that grounded me, you know? Things that made me feel like *me* when I wasn't at the clinic. I've always been an avid birdwatcher and gardener. I have this whole setup in my backyard—multiple feeders, specific seed mixes for different seasons, a birdbath I clean religiously. And my garden... I usually spend the whole winter planning what I'm going to plant in the spring, ordering seeds, sketching out layouts. I even bought this beautiful macro lens for my camera last year so I could take close-up photos of the pollinators and the blooms. 

But lately? I haven't even touched the camera. It's just sitting in its case on the shelf gathering dust. And the bird feeders... I think they've been empty for weeks now. I look out the window and I see the squirrels have knocked one over, and I just... I don't care. I don't care at all. I don't care what birds are migrating through, I don't care what's coming up in the garden. The daffodils came up a few weeks ago, and usually I'd be out there with my coffee, just so happy to see them, taking pictures, but this year I just looked at them and felt absolutely nothing. Just this heavy, blank emptiness. It's honestly really frightening, because like I said, those things used to be how I felt like myself. It's like I don't even know who I am if I don't care about the birds or the garden, but I just can't summon the energy or the interest to go out there. Even when my friends call to ask if I want to go to the botanical gardens—which we used to do all the time—I just make up an excuse. I just want to sit in my chair and stare at the wall. It's just... nothing brings me any joy right now. Nothing at all.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Yes, absolutely. It's... it's exactly like you said, most of the day, nearly every single day. And it's definitely been going on for way longer than two weeks. It's just this constant, heavy, suffocating feeling that I carry around with me from the moment I wake up until I finally manage to fall asleep. 

Like I was saying before about the garden, it's just like all the color has drained out of everything. And it doesn't even matter what's going on around me. My house can be completely chaotic—my husband trying to fix something in the kitchen, the dogs barking because the mail carrier is outside, the TV blaring in the living room—and I'm just sitting there in the middle of it all, feeling completely isolated and just so overwhelmingly sad. I try to hide it, I really do, because my husband gets so worried, and I don't want to burden him with this when he's already working so hard. So, what I do is, I'll make an excuse to go do a chore. I'll say I need to switch the laundry, and I'll go into the laundry room and shut the door. And I just sit there on the floor next to the dryer, and I just cry. I cry until I can't breathe, just sobbing because I feel so incredibly hopeless and I can't stand the thought of anyone seeing me like that. 

And then I have to splash cold water on my face and try to pull myself together before I go back out there, but the feeling never actually leaves. It's just this dark cloud that follows me everywhere, every single day. I can't remember the last time I woke up and actually felt light, or hopeful, or just... normal. It's just this heavy, dark sadness, all day, every day.
Have you ever felt this way before, like you were sinking into a deep sadness that didn’t go away for weeks or longer?

Well, it’s funny you ask if I’ve felt this way *before*, because... honestly, it feels like this isn't really a 'before and after' situation. It's just been this one, long, unending stretch. This whole thing, this... this depression, it’s been hanging over me for about 11 months now. 

Yeah, 11 months. I remember exactly when I started noticing it, because it was right around the time we were doing our big annual inventory and deep clean at the clinic, which is always an absolute nightmare of a week, but I usually just power through it with lots of coffee and a good attitude. But last year, I just felt this massive weight settle over me right in the middle of it. And I kept thinking, you know, once inventory is done, I'll bounce back. I just need to get through the week. But I didn't bounce back. And then I thought, well, maybe when I can spend more time outside, I'll feel better. But like I said, I didn't even care about being outside. So I just kept dragging myself through the days, week after week, month after month. 

So it’s been there, just hanging over me, coloring every single interaction, every single day for almost a whole year. But for a long time, it was... manageable, I guess? Or at least, I was managing to hide it from my husband and my coworkers. I could fake a smile for the clients when they brought their pets in, even if I felt dead inside. 

But then this past month... I don't even know what shifted, I really don't, but this past month just made everything feel completely unbearable. That's when it stopped just being a dark cloud and turned into this... this suffocating force. That's when the thoughts about the highway started, like I mentioned earlier. For those first ten months, I was just incredibly, deeply sad and empty, but this last month... it's like I can't even tread water anymore. I'm just drowning in it. I try to trace it back, try to figure out why this month is so much worse than the months before it, but I just can't figure it out. It's just gotten so heavy I can't hold it up anymore.
Have you ever had a period of time before this one—lasting at least a couple of months—where you felt like yourself again, without this kind of depression weighing on you?

I... gosh, I honestly don't know. I really don't. It’s so strange, but when I try to think back to before that inventory week last year, it’s like trying to look through muddy water. I mean, I know logically that I must have had times where I was okay, right? Because I bought that macro lens for my camera, and I used to be the one who organized the clinic’s holiday party every December—coordinating the potluck, doing the secret Santa, making sure all the vets and the other techs had a nice time. You don't do things like that if you're completely miserable. But when I try to actually pinpoint a couple of months where I just felt like *me*, where I was completely free of this... this weight? I just draw a total blank. I'm really not sure. 

It's like this current heaviness has just retroactively erased my memory of ever being light. I was actually looking at some photos on my phone the other night when I couldn't sleep, and I found these pictures from two years ago. My husband and I went to a continuing education conference in Denver, and we tacked on a few days to go hiking in the Rockies. There's this one picture of me smiling on a trail, holding my binoculars. And I look at it, and I can't actually *remember* what I was feeling in that moment. I can't tell if I was genuinely happy and feeling like myself, or if I was just going through the motions back then, too, and just hiding it better. 

It's so frustrating because I want to give you a clear timeline. I know you need to know these things to help me, but I just... I haven't noticed a clear break. I can't remember a solid block of time where I can look back and say, 'Yes, I was exactly myself then.' It just feels like I've been tired and heavy for a very, very long time, and I just can't see past it to whatever came before.
